title: DFS in Hanoi: Find a Path Deeper First!
description: Watch DFS explore Hanoi’s street network by going deeper before it backtracks. This reel visualizes how depth-first search navigates a graph of intersections to reach a destination.
ig_caption:
🗺️✨ DFS in Hanoi (Ba Đình) looks like a student map-sketching instinctively: go deep first, then backtrack. 

🔬 **DFS (Depth-First Search)** treats the city as a **graph**—intersections are nodes, streets are edges. Using a **stack / recursion**, DFS keeps moving to an unvisited neighbor until it hits a dead end, then it rewinds and tries the next unexplored branch. 

📌 On real street maps, that “deeper-first” behavior can quickly discover a route in some layouts, but it may also wander far from the target because it optimizes **exploration order**, not shortest distance. 

⚙️ **Graph theory takeaway:** DFS is a systematic traversal of connected components; with a visited set, it prevents cycles and ensures each node is processed at most once.
